hacker_news.title: LLMs .what do you smoke beforehand?
hacker_news.author: kderbyma
hacker_news.content_context:
I know this is going to sound negative, and probably a bit generalist but....seriously, what exactly is the LLM helping you with that is not just purely "time saving" - ie. Actual, novel work.

I personally feel like while I cannot prove it, nor want to frankly, that LLMs have been neutered intentionally since around October of last year. 4.5-4.6 Opus....

Every single company has degraded their models eirher intentionally or accidentally(probably worse) and they cannot admit it and will gaslight you if you even try to acknowledge it....but for my own experiments, LLMs are actually worse than no-LLM....

I dont see anyone building anything they couldnt have done before hand....and I am seeing stuff that didnt need to be made...much more frequently....to the degree that I cannot remember the last good idea I have seen even on here (whereas there were cool ideas every month posted here)...

I also cannot get even mediocre output anymore...Its literally just trash - Literally a prompt to dumpster pipeline....

Clause is the worst. Hands down. They have regressed on every single model since 4.5....to rhe degree that 4.5 when it was released was hands down better than anythingg...

hacker_news.title: AI usage patterns in software teams
hacker_news.author: giuliomagnifico
hacker_news.summary: AI usage patterns in software teams: who is adopting AI, how it reshapes where teams spend their time, and how much more they ship.

linked_context.page_description: AI usage patterns in software teams: who is adopting AI, how it reshapes where teams spend their time, and how much more they ship.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
Tens of thousands of teams build software inside Linear every day. Over six years that’s given us a detailed picture of how product development happens, from before AI was widely adopted to now.

Model companies and coding tools have published plenty on token usage and code volume, but that captures only one layer of the work. We’re unusually well placed to see the entire workflow behind building a product, from the first issue to the pull request that closes it. What we can’t see is AI usage that happens outside Linear, so this is a picture of adoption inside our own customer base, not...

We look at three things across that transition. Who is using AI, how it reshapes where teams spend their time across Linear, and whether it changes how much they ship. Together they make a fixed point for where AI-assisted product development stands in 2026, and something to measure the next edition against.

hacker_news.title: Show HN: Draw.city – geography game where you circle the target population [US]
hacker_news.author: NameError
hacker_news.summary: Draw a map area to match today’s target population. See your score, try the center bonus, then play past challenges.

linked_context.page_description: Draw a map area to match today’s target population. See your score, try the center bonus, then play past challenges.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
Select Draw your area or hide this panel. Then trace one complete outline.

A census block reports a total. It does not say where inside it those people live. Place everyone in each census block at its southern edge and the median line falls as far south as the data permits. Place them at the northern edge and it falls as far north. Any line between the two could be the true median. East and west work the same way. The band covers that range.

We weigh over 2020 census blocks when an area holds at most 25,000 of them, and over census tracts above that. Tracts are larger than blocks, so weighing over tracts gives a wider band. The width reflects the size of the weighing unit, not the distribution of people.

hacker_news.content_context:
The core idea is, you draw a circle on a satellite view map and it tells you the population inside + more info.

The home page is a daily challenge, I've backfilled some "past challenges" so there's more than just the past couple of days to play, and there is also a free-draw mode that tells you population + some census demographic info & points-of-interest data from OpenStreetMap.

In most cases, the data comes from taking the census blocks w/ centroids contained in your circle and summing their population. Demographic info is slightly more complex as it's not sourced on blocks, so we allocate population-weighted fractions of a source territory's published census values into the drawn territory. Happy to answer any questions about the data or the technical side. The game/app only covers US areas at the moment, I'd like to add international data in the future!

hacker_news.title: Tail: A 0–5 scale for how much AI wrote this
hacker_news.author: beaucronin
hacker_news.summary: Labeling work product to clarify human / AI authorship
comment_highlights: Why does it matter if code is written by LLM?

linked_context.page_description: Labeling work product to clarify human / AI authorship
linked_context.page_excerpt:
It is a good thing to label our work according to how much AI assistance we used. Here is a simple labeling system that is useful to me. I hope it will be useful to you, too.

As a consultant who helps businesses apply AI to improve their workflows, I use AI tools to varying degrees depending on the job. I am comfortable using AI aggressively in some places, and I am much more reticent in others. I realize that other people have different sensibilities – and that norms are changing very quickly!

What I haven’t seen, and what I want, are quick and easy labels to bring transparency. Not knowing how something was produced can cause a lot of confusion, or worse.

hacker_news.title: Mapping art styles onto Scott McCloud's Big Triangle with multimodal models
hacker_news.author: punchlineinthef
hacker_news.summary: 365 looks on one triangle — McCloud’s Big Triangle made explorable, style neighborhoods, and a validation check of how vision models place art next to the original map.

linked_context.page_title: Pokémon, Picasso, and the Language of Comics: Can AI Map Art Styles to Purpose?
linked_context.page_description: 365 looks on one triangle — McCloud’s Big Triangle made explorable, style neighborhoods, and a validation check of how vision models place art next to the original map.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
We put Pokémon and Picasso on McCloud’s Big Triangle to ask: can comic language describe vision — and can AI map art styles to purpose? Inspired by Understanding Comics .

Scott McCloud’s Big Triangle places pictures between Reality , Language , and Picture . The Style Atlas maps 365 looks there. The published map uses the tagging results of the gated repair v3 prompt with Gemini 3.7 Flash . Typical miss on the data validation test is ~8% on ten comics (McCloud’s whole printed set ~13% ; zero landmarks ~15% ). Franchises skew Language ; artists stay more Reality...

Sits with Qwen and Kimi; several models can still share “#1.”

top_trends.author: giuliomagnifico
top_trends.summary: AI usage patterns in software teams: who is adopting AI, how it reshapes where teams spend their time, and how much more they ship.

linked_context.page_description: AI usage patterns in software teams: who is adopting AI, how it reshapes where teams spend their time, and how much more they ship.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
Tens of thousands of teams build software inside Linear every day. Over six years that’s given us a detailed picture of how product development happens, from before AI was widely adopted to now.

Model companies and coding tools have published plenty on token usage and code volume, but that captures only one layer of the work. We’re unusually well placed to see the entire workflow behind building a product, from the first issue to the pull request that closes it. What we can’t see is AI usage that happens outside Linear, so this is a picture of adoption inside our own customer base, not...

We look at three things across that transition. Who is using AI, how it reshapes where teams spend their time across Linear, and whether it changes how much they ship. Together they make a fixed point for where AI-assisted product development stands in 2026, and something to measure the next edition against.

top_trends.title: Show HN: Draw.city – geography game where you circle the target population [US]
top_trends.author: NameError
top_trends.summary: Draw a map area to match today’s target population. See your score, try the center bonus, then play past challenges.

linked_context.page_description: Draw a map area to match today’s target population. See your score, try the center bonus, then play past challenges.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
Select Draw your area or hide this panel. Then trace one complete outline.

A census block reports a total. It does not say where inside it those people live. Place everyone in each census block at its southern edge and the median line falls as far south as the data permits. Place them at the northern edge and it falls as far north. Any line between the two could be the true median. East and west work the same way. The band covers that range.

We weigh over 2020 census blocks when an area holds at most 25,000 of them, and over census tracts above that. Tracts are larger than blocks, so weighing over tracts gives a wider band. The width reflects the size of the weighing unit, not the distribution of people.

top_trends.content_context:
The core idea is, you draw a circle on a satellite view map and it tells you the population inside + more info.

The home page is a daily challenge, I've backfilled some "past challenges" so there's more than just the past couple of days to play, and there is also a free-draw mode that tells you population + some census demographic info & points-of-interest data from OpenStreetMap.

In most cases, the data comes from taking the census blocks w/ centroids contained in your circle and summing their population. Demographic info is slightly more complex as it's not sourced on blocks, so we allocate population-weighted fractions of a source territory's published census values into the drawn territory. Happy to answer any questions about the data or the technical side. The game/app only covers US areas at the moment, I'd like to add international data in the future!

named_hotspots.what_happened: Basecamp 团队在 GitHub 上发布了一个名为 Omarchy 的 Linux 发行版项目，该项目因其“美观、现代且具有鲜明观点”的设计理念而迅速走红，单日获得 411 颗星，总星数已达 26388。
named_hotspots.core_details: Omarchy 是一个使用 Shell 语言编写的 Linux 发行版项目，由 Basecamp 团队（包括 dhh、ryanrhughes 等知名开发者）构建。它强调美观、现代的用户界面和一套预设的、固执己见的系统配置与工具选择，旨在提供开箱即用的优质开发者体验。
named_hotspots.ai_take: 该项目本身并非 AI 模型，但其开发团队中包含了“claude”，这可能指代 AI 助手 Claude 的贡献，或仅是同名开发者。这反映了当前开源项目中，AI 辅助编码或 AI 生成代码（如 Shell 脚本）正逐渐成为一种常见的协作或工具化模式。
named_hotspots.hype_check: 热度较高。项目在 GitHub Trending 上趋势得分达 78.68，单日涨星显著，表明其在开发者社区中引起了广泛关注和兴趣，尤其是来自 Basecamp 团队和其“观点鲜明”的设计理念的吸引力。
named_hotspots.value_check: 对于寻求高度定制化、美观且预配置完善的 Linux 桌面或开发环境的用户具有实用价值。它降低了手动配置复杂系统的门槛，提供了经过精心筛选的工具链和界面。价值在于其“固执己见”的预设，这可能节省高级用户的时间，但也可能不适合喜欢完全自主配置的用户。
named_hotspots.follow_up: 关注其后续版本更新，看是否集成更多 AI 辅助开发工具或智能化系统管理特性。同时，观察社区反馈，了解其在实际使用中的稳定性和与现有生态的兼容性。
named_hotspots.evidence: 项目描述明确为“美观、现代且具有鲜明观点的 Linux”，语言为 Shell，由 Basecamp 团队构建。GitHub 数据：单日星数 411，总星数 26388，趋势分数 78.68。

named_hotspots.name: PLFM_RADAR
named_hotspots.what_happened: 一个名为PLFM_RADAR的开源、低成本10.5 GHz PLFM相控阵雷达系统项目在GitHub上趋势飙升，单日获得204颗星，总星数已达24275。
named_hotspots.core_details: 该项目由NawfalMotii79等开发者主导，使用PLSQL语言编写，旨在提供可访问的相控阵雷达技术方案。
named_hotspots.ai_take: 开源雷达系统可能为AI驱动的感知、自动驾驶或无人机导航提供低成本硬件基础，促进边缘AI与雷达数据融合的创新应用。
named_hotspots.hype_check: 趋势热度较高（趋势得分78.41），但需注意其技术成熟度和实际部署挑战，开源项目常处于实验阶段。
named_hotspots.value_check: 若项目能持续维护并验证性能，可降低雷达技术门槛，对研究、教育和工业原型开发具有实用价值。
named_hotspots.follow_up: 关注其文档完善度、社区活跃度及实际测试案例，以评估是否适合集成到AI感知系统中。
named_hotspots.evidence: GitHub项目页面显示详细描述、星数增长及贡献者信息，但缺少页面摘要或用户评论亮点作为额外佐证。

named_hotspots.name: OpenViking
named_hotspots.what_happened: 火山引擎开源项目OpenViking登上GitHub趋势榜，今日获298星，总星数达29318。
named_hotspots.core_details: OpenViking是一个为AI智能体设计的自演进上下文数据库，旨在统一智能体的记忆、知识检索增强生成（RAG）和技能。项目由火山引擎团队开发，主要使用Python语言。
named_hotspots.ai_take: 该项目通过构建统一的上下文数据库，试图解决AI智能体在长期记忆、知识管理和技能复用方面的核心挑战，可能推动智能体架构向更模块化、可演进的方向发展。
named_hotspots.hype_check: 项目热度较高（趋势得分77.61），总星数近3万且持续增长，表明开发者社区对其概念和技术方向有较强兴趣。
named_hotspots.value_check: 作为开源基础设施，若能实现其宣称的“自演进”和“统一”目标，可降低构建复杂AI智能体的门槛，但实际效果需观察大规模应用案例。
named_hotspots.follow_up: 关注其版本迭代是否解决智能体记忆一致性问题，以及与其他主流智能体框架（如LangChain）的集成生态。
named_hotspots.evidence: 项目描述明确其定位为“Self-evolving Context Database for AI Agents”，GitHub数据（今日298星、总29318星、2303评论）反映社区活跃度。

named_hotspots.name: omlx
named_hotspots.what_happened: 一个名为omlx的LLM推理服务器项目在GitHub上趋势飙升，今日新增366颗星，总星数达19371。该项目专为Apple Silicon设计，提供连续批处理和SSD缓存功能，并可通过macOS菜单栏管理。
named_hotspots.core_details: omlx是一个用Python编写的开源项目，由jundot等人开发。它作为LLM推理服务器，针对Apple Silicon硬件优化，支持连续批处理以提高效率，并利用SSD进行缓存以加速推理。其独特之处在于提供了macOS菜单栏的集成管理界面，便于用户直接控制。
named_hotspots.ai_take: 该项目反映了在边缘设备（特别是苹果生态）上高效部署LLM的强烈需求。通过连续批处理和SSD缓存，它可能显著降低延迟和资源消耗，使个人开发者或小团队能在本地运行更复杂的模型。菜单栏集成则降低了使用门槛，促进了AI工具的平民化。
named_hotspots.hype_check: 趋势得分77.48和单日高星增长表明社区关注度快速上升，但需注意这可能部分源于苹果开发者社群的集中兴趣。作为较新的项目，其生产环境稳定性和长期维护性仍有待观察。
named_hotspots.value_check: 对于拥有Apple Silicon设备的AI开发者或研究者，omlx提供了轻量级、易管理的本地推理解决方案，可能节省云服务成本并提升隐私性。其开源性质允许自定义优化，但性能提升的实际幅度需在实际使用中验证。
named_hotspots.follow_up: 关注项目后续版本更新，特别是对更多模型架构的支持和性能基准测试。可尝试在M1/M2/M3芯片的Mac上部署，评估其在不同模型规模下的实际效率。
named_hotspots.evidence: 项目GitHub页面描述其为“LLM inference server with continuous batching & SSD caching for Apple Silicon — managed from the macOS menu bar”，语言为Python，总星数19371，今日增长366星，由jundot等贡献者维护。

source_briefs.content_summary: 这是一个免费的公共API集合列表项目，使用Python语言编写。今日新增星标1139个，总星标数已达464450。项目由多位贡献者共同维护。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 该项目是开发者寻找和集成第三方服务的经典资源库，持续的高关注度反映了市场对标准化API接口的稳定需求。

source_briefs.content_summary: 该项目利用AI大模型和自动化工作流，实现根据主题或关键词一键生成高清短视频的功能。使用Python语言，今日新增星标2306个，总星标数108434。
source_briefs.ai_comment: AI视频生成工具热度不减，该项目将多模态大模型与工作流自动化结合，降低了短视频创作门槛，是AIGC应用落地的典型代表。

source_briefs.content_summary: 这是一个功能齐全的下载管理器，使用TypeScript语言开发。今日新增星标607个，总星标数53620。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 跨平台、高性能的下载工具始终有市场需求，该项目在开源社区保持活跃，说明对现代化、可扩展下载解决方案的需求持续存在。

source_briefs.content_summary: 用户对LLM（大语言模型）的实际效用提出质疑，认为其目前主要只是节省时间，而非创造新颖工作。用户感觉自去年10月以来，各大公司的模型（如Claude 4.5-4.6 Opus）性能有意或无意地出现了退化，输出质量低下，且近期未见基于LLM的真正创新应用出现。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 这反映了部分开发者对当前LLM发展进入平台期或出现性能回退的担忧，触及了AI工具在超越“效率工具”迈向“创造力增强”过程中遇到的瓶颈问题。

source_briefs.item_name: Show HN: Roost – top for your Claude Code sessions
source_briefs.content_summary: Roost是一个用于监控Claude Code（Claude的编程功能）会话的工具，类似于系统监控命令‘top’。它能显示实时会话、使用的模型、消耗的上下文长度以及会话生成的子代理（subagents）。该项目为单文件、无依赖的Python脚本，支持多平台。会话会按“忽略成本”分组显示，例如即将停止工作的“接近限制”会话或下次调用将计费整个上下文的“停放+昂贵”会话。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 该工具针对AI编程助手的资源管理和成本监控需求，显示了随着AI深度集成到开发工作流中，对使用过程进行可视化和优化的细分工具开始出现。

source_briefs.item_name: AI usage patterns in software teams
source_briefs.content_summary: 基于项目管理工具Linear对其数万用户团队的数据分析，报告揭示了2026年软件团队中AI的使用模式。研究聚焦于三个层面：哪些人在使用AI、AI如何重塑团队在Linear内的时间分配、以及AI是否改变了团队的产出量。报告旨在为AI辅助的产品开发现状提供一个基准。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 这份来自真实工作流平台的数据分析，超越了单纯的代码生成量统计，试图从整体工作流程和效率提升角度量化AI对软件开发的影响，具有较高的参考价值。

source_briefs.item_name: Trump’s Ballroom Is Rising at Breakneck Speed: 20 Hours a Day, 7 Days a Week - The New York Times
source_briefs.content_summary: 《纽约时报》头条报道，特朗普的舞厅项目正以每周7天、每天20小时的速度快速推进。相关报道还涉及最高法院可能利用此案削弱环境法、项目反对者要求最高法院暂停项目，以及辩称国会已批准该白宫项目等内容。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 此政治事件涉及司法、行政与环境政策的交叉，其高速推进可能旨在造成既定事实，相关法律博弈值得关注。

source_briefs.item_name: Trump is weighing whether to grant Canada a tariff reprieve - Politico
source_briefs.content_summary: Politico报道，特朗普正在考虑是否给予加拿大关税豁免。相关报道聚焦于加拿大避免美国新关税的最后期限临近，美国方面淡化最后一刻达成协议的可能性，以及美国企业主在潜在50%关税下面临的供应链抉择。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 美加贸易关系再次面临关键节点，关税决策将直接影响双边供应链和商业利益，体现了贸易政策的不确定性。

source_briefs.item_name: Trump seeks to open millions of acres of national forests to roads - The Washington Post
source_briefs.content_summary: 《华盛顿邮报》报道，特朗普政府寻求开放数百万英亩的国家森林用于修建道路，并推进废除国家森林的“无路规则”（roadless rule），以开放伐木业。相关报道还涉及撤销保护古老森林的规则，以及农业部声称此举旨在缓解日益增长的野火风险。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 此举是环境政策与资源开发利益之间的重大冲突，可能对国家森林生态系统和环境保护法律体系产生深远影响。

summary.closing_note: 总体来看，今日热点反映了AI技术正加速与具体工作流、硬件平台及专业领域（如网络安全）深度融合的趋势。开源社区在降低AI应用门槛、提供模块化组件方面持续发力，但项目的长期价值仍需在实际部署与生态整合中验证。开发者可重点关注那些旨在解决AI智能体记忆、边缘推理效率及跨平台技能标准化等核心挑战的项目，它们可能塑造未来的AI开发范式。
